MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 28, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on February 28, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 23, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation: (Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9) Steven Goodridge v. City of Mission Viejo: OCSC Case No. 30-2015-
  00800194-CU-EI-CJC

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Property: 26836 Oso Parkway, Mission
  Viejo Agency Negotiators; Dennis Wilberg, William Curley, and Elaine Lister:
  Negotiating Party: Jamboree Housing Under Negotiations Terms for Previously
  Approved Refinancing.
City Council Minutes  1  February 28, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session items CS1 and CS2 staff was given
direction but in neither case was there action to report.

INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PUBLIC COMMENTS

John Rodriguez, M.V.: announced that he is a home loan specialist and pro beach volleyball
official and he is pleased to be a new member of the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce.

Jessica Frausto, M.V: expressed concern that Mission Viejo Christian Church was charged only
$25 to rent a park and generator for a National Day of Prayer event.

The following asked Mayor Bucknum to provide a recap of her recent meeting with
Congresswoman Mimi Walters: Amy Stevens, M.V.; Kailey Wright, M.V.; James Renzas, M.V.;
Jessica Riegert, M.V.; Andrea Rangno, M.V.; Caitness Rodriguez, M.V.; and Barbara Scheinman,
M.V.

Dee Alford, M.V.: expressed concern with parking in her neighborhood and asked the City to
restrict parking on one side of San Doval Lane during school hours, Monday through Friday from
7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Nicole Inamine, M.V.: expressed concern with the lack of street lighting near her home at
Camden/Felipe and stated that she feels unsafe walking home at night. She also discussed drainage
issues in the Camden neighborhood.

Steven Lamont, M.V.: Board Member for the South Orange County Economic Coalition, Irvine:
announced that the 3rd annual South Orange County Economic Report event will be held on March
10 at Saddleback College in the Student Services Center from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.

The following expressed concern about the future of the Outta Bounds program and asked the City
Council to continue to provide space for the program at the Potocki Center: Natasha Landrum,
M.V.; Samantha Apodaca, M.V.; Joey Likar, M.V.; Nihar, Lauren and Samantha Mehta, M.V.;
Denise and Ben Liker, M.V.; Maya Apodaca, M.V.; Jennifer Posey, M.V.; and Scott Ramirez,
Rancho Santa Margarita.

City Council Minutes  2  February 28, 2017
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the Budget Workshop of February 2, 2017, as presented; and
  (2) approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 14, 2017, as
  presented.

3.  Claim Against the City - Mehrdadi

  Rejected Claim.

4.  Check Register Dated February 3, 2017 in the Amount of $690,157.44

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated February 10, 2017 in the Amount of $976,361.13

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Quarterly Check Register Report – Second Quarter of FY 2016-17

  Received and filed.

7.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  – For the Six Months Ended December 31, 2016

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  February 28, 2017
 8.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter of 2016-17

  Received and filed.

9.  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 17837)

  Adopted Resolution 17-05 Approving and Authorizing Execution of a Grant Agreement
  Between the California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery and the City of
  Mission Viejo and Amending the Fiscal Year 2016-2017 Budget for Costs Related to
  Capital Improvement Project 837.

10.  Local Transit Circulator Planning Study (CIP 17235)

  (1) Adopted Resolution 17-06 Amending the Fiscal Year 2016-17 Budget to Create Capital
  Improvement Project 17235 to study potential local circulator transit routes; and (2)
  awarded a contract to Moore & Associates, Inc., in the amount of $48,737 to perform a
  planning study for potential local circulator transit routes.

11.  General Plan Progress Report for 2016

  Received and filed report.

12.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) and City Council: Approval of
  Implementation Agreements to Complete the Previously Approved CDBG Program
  Project

  (1) Adopted Joint Resolution 17-07 of the City Council and Housing Authority Approving
  the Cooperation Agreement (CDBG Funds Transfer for Families Forward Affordable
  Housing Project) for Transfer of $820,000 of CDBG Funds to Implement the CDBG
  Subrecipient Loan and Affordable Housing Agreement, and Making Certain Other
  Findings; and (2) adopted Housing Authority Resolution 17-01 Approving the CDBG
  Subrecipient Loan and Affordable Housing Agreement between the Housing Authority and
  Families Forward to Provide a CDBG Loan for Acquisition and Long-Term Operation of
  Two Single-Family Homes for Tenancy and Occupancy by Qualified Very Low Income
  Households, and Making Certain Other Findings.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13. Planning and Transportation Commission Vacancy

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint Jo
  Anne Simon to serve on the Planning and Transportation Commission.

City Council Minutes  4  February 28, 2017
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

15. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

16. Legislative Update

  The City Council received the legislative update from Cori Williams of Townsend Public
  Affairs.

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg drew the Council’s attention to a memo from Assistant City Manager
Rattay identifying a slope failure along Oso Creek. The failure is in the vicinity of the Celebration
Garden and Rotary Club Garden, just north of the bridge that crosses the creek. There has been
significant wash out and Santa Margarita Water District will be surveying the area while the City
obtains a bid for repairs from Bistline Construction. City Manager Wilberg said the Council can
direct staff to immediately begin the work under an emergency Purchase Order or staff can return
to the City Council with a cost proposal at a special meeting.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to direct staff
to proceed with the corrective work and return to the City Council to ratify the expenses at the next
Council Meeting.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

17. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  The City Council received the report from Battalion Chief John Abel.

City Council Minutes  5  February 28, 2017
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The following asked Mayor Bucknum to reveal the topics discussed at her recent meeting
  with Congresswoman Mimi Walters: Kailey Wright, M.V.; James Renzas, M.V.; and Amy
  Stevens, M.V.

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that South Mission Viejo Little League is celebrating its 50th
anniversary and he noted that he played in the league in 1969 and 1970 so it was fun to attend their
special opening day celebration. He also attended the softball opening day ceremonies as well as
the Community Health Fair and the Volunteer Luncheon. Council Member Goodell said that he
attended the Mayor’s public safety Town Hall meeting and he provided a reminder to residents
that the next Community Emergency Preparedness Academy (CEPA) begins on April 18. CEPA
is designed to help people prepare themselves and their neighborhoods for a catastrophic event
and he encouraged residents to look for information on the City’s website and sign up.

Council Member Kelley

In response to the comments made during item 18, Council Member Kelley informed the residents
that the report contained in the agenda is really just a record of what meetings the Council Members
attended so they can obtain reimbursement for their mileage. She discussed cleanup after the recent
rain storm and thanked staff for their hard work to keep the City clean and safe. Council Member
Kelley outlined her attendance at recent events including the 35th anniversary celebration for
Sunrise Senior Living, two Little League opening days, a girls’ softball opening day, the
Community Health Fair and the City’s volunteer recognition. She thanked the many individuals
who have provided over $800,000 worth of free work for the City and she stated that volunteers
make it possible for the City to do so much more. Council Member Kelley complimented Mayor
Bucknum on a very well done Town Hall meeting on public safety and she announced that
Assembly Member Bill Brough and Senator Pat Bates will host two upcoming events for seniors:
a resource fair called “Senior Day” on March 10, 2017, from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at the Murray
Community Center and a Veterans Resource Fair in conjunction with the Wounded Warriors
Amputee Softball Game on March 25 at Saddleback College.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths expressed appreciation to those who made public comments at tonight’s
meeting. He stated that he is serving in his third year on the City Council and Congresswoman
Mimi Walters has yet to come to Mission Viejo to speak to the residents. He noted that when he
City Council Minutes  6  February 28, 2017
 ran against Mrs. Walters for Congress she would not debate him and she spent over $1 million
attacking him as a veteran. Council Member Raths said that Mimi Walters is the wrong person for
Mission Viejo because she lives in another Congressional District and he feels that it is time for
her to come out and listen to the residents.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that he too will be attending the Southern California Association
of Governments (SCAG) meeting in May as Chairman of the Foothill Eastern Toll Road Agency
and on behalf of the TCA. He also announced that he substituted for the Mayor at the South Orange
County Community College District 50th anniversary celebration and he was proud to stand in and
present the City's proclamation. He reminded residents that if they have issues and comments
regarding parking and street lights, they should make comments before the Planning and
Transportation Commission which meets on the second Monday of the month. The Commission
also has a traffic committee that will hear issues about parking restrictions and speed bumps.
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs discussed a recent incident in the Senate in Sacramento when Senator Janet
Nguyen was removed from the chamber while speaking about the Vietnam War. He noted that
Senator Nguyen had family members killed in Vietnam, she is an immigrant and simply wished to
share another side of the story. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said that people behaved abhorrently by not
allowing her to speak and he noted that some of the Senators apologized to her later.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum outlined her attendance at the Orange County Fire Authority Best and Bravest
award ceremony where Mission Viejo firefighter Robby Bosanko was honored as Battalion 7
Firefighter of the Year. She also attended an Eagle Scout Court of Honor for Ryan Hales and
Zachary Beckett and she noted that scouts do quite a few projects throughout the City so it was a
special honor to recognize them. Mayor Bucknum discussed last night’s Town Hall meeting which
covered law enforcement, fire resources, crime prevention and Neighborhood Watch. She said the
meeting was well attended and the City will try to hold additional Town Halls this year, focusing
on a single subject. Mayor Bucknum reminded residents of the upcoming Wounded Warrior
Amputee Softball Game and she thanked Victor and Eileen Gonzalez who originally brought the
Wounded Warriors to Mission Viejo. In closing, the Mayor announced that she would adjourn the
meeting in memory of one of the City’s longtime police services volunteers, Cliff McKinley.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:07 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Cliff McKinley, to Tuesday, March 14,
2017, at 5:00 p.m.

_______________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk  Approved at the meeting of March 14, 2017

City Council Minutes  7  February 28, 2017
